body:
## Summary
The pipeline has three aging clocks that disagree: the board and sidebar badge age a card by its stage ROLE's SLA (offer 3 d, interview 5 d, terminal never), while the automation policy pass that writes `stale_alert`/`aging_alert` into the activity feed uses one flat 21/30-day cut for every stage, including Hired. Make one TS module the only source of the aging tier, hand the tier to Python, and write each alert once per stage stint.

## Description
Today an offer turns amber on the board on day 3 but the feed says nothing until day 21, and then says it every business day. A hired candidate (status stays `active`) gets an `aging_alert` in the feed every day from day 30 on, forever — the registry's terminal-stages-never-age failure, at the source of the computation. The feed's verb says "past the stage SLA" although the writer never read one, and the soft/hard tier names are inverted between the board and the engine.

The move: `app/_lib/aging-policy.ts` exports `agingTier(stage, daysInStage, axis, overrides?) -> none|aging|stalled` over the existing `slaForStage` + a single `STALLED_MULTIPLE` (2x, per the technique). `agingBucket` (board) and `attentionCounts` (badge) delegate to it; `listActiveEntriesForAutomation` stamps `agingTier` per entry from that entry's OWN workspace axis (axis cached per workspace for the pass); `evaluate_entry` maps aging->stale_alert, stalled->aging_alert, never alerts on a terminal stage, and falls back to its flat POLICY only when the tier is absent (CLI/back-compat). The commit loop dedupes aging alerts on `stage_changed_at` (once per stint per tier) instead of per business day. Event kinds are unchanged (persisted rows keep reading); only the four-locale verbs are reworded to name their tier.

## Flow
1. Add aging-policy.ts + its test (tier table, terminal rule, parity fixture against agingBucket).
2. Delegate agingBucket and attention.ts to it — byte-identical on the shipped axis.
3. Enrich automation entries with agingTier; add `hasEventSinceStageChange` beside hasEventToday.
4. Python: consume agingTier, move the terminal guard ahead of alerts, keep the flat fallback; extend test_automation.py.
5. Swap the alert dedupe in automation-pass.ts; pin it in automation-pass.test.ts.
6. Reword the two verbs in en/cs/de/fr (both namespaces), update the two pipeline docs.

## Expected impact
The feed, the badge and the board give one answer to "is this candidate waiting too long": an offer ignored for 4 days produces an alert instead of silence, a hire produces none, and a stalled row produces one entry per stint instead of a daily line that buries the feed. Closes a whole class (every future stage/axis change now moves all three surfaces together).

## Evaluation
Claim: aging alerts are written from the same stage-role SLA the board renders, never for a terminal stage, once per stage stint.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: contract
Result: pending build
Gate: contract

title: Commit the pass you previewed: per-row opt-out and a changed-since-preview report
acceptance: planCommit(fresh=[advance e1 Screened->Interview], approved=[{entryId:e1, action:'advance', toStage:'Interview'}]) -> e1 verdict 'apply'

body:
## Summary
The policy pass's look-before-commit modal previews a list and then commits something else: the Apply button re-runs the whole pass with no reference to what was shown, applies all of it or nothing, and — when only other teams have changes — applies theirs. Make the commit carry the recruiter's reviewed selection, apply only rows that still match what was shown, and report the ones that changed.

## Description
Today the preview is advisory. Between the dry run and the click the pass is recomputed, so a candidate whose score landed in between can be advanced without ever appearing in the modal, a row the recruiter disagrees with cannot be held back without abandoning the whole pass, and a join onto an in-flight clock pass returns someone else's result as if it were this click's. That is the hitl-approval failure 'what runs on approval is not what was shown'.

The leap: each advance and would-be-reject row gets a checkbox (default on). Commit posts `approved: [{entryId, action, toStage}]`. A pure `automation-commit-plan.ts` reconciles the fresh decisions against it per entry: `apply` (same action and target), `declined` (unticked, absent, or another team's), `drifted` (the pass now decides differently). Declined/drifted decisions are not applied and persist as outcome 'skipped' with reasonCode `notApproved` / `changedSincePreview`; alerts and holds stay autonomous. The modal's commit result lists drifted rows with a Re-preview action; a joined pass answers `selectionHonored:false` and says so. Calls without `approved` keep today's behaviour exactly.

## Flow
1. automation-commit-plan.ts + tests (the four verdicts, workspace scoping, validation).
2. runAutomationPass({ approved }) consults the plan in the commit loop; two new PassReasonCodes.
3. Route: validate `approved` (400 AUTOMATION_SELECTION_INVALID), scope it to the caller's workspace, return `drifted` + `selectionHonored`.
4. PassPreviewModal: per-row checkboxes, 'Apply N selected', post-commit drift list; drop the apply-other-teams branch when a selection is sent.
5. useAutomationPass/SimControlDock pass the selection through.
6. Catalog keys in four locales; the pipeline doc's automation section.

## Expected impact
The one human checkpoint on unattended advances becomes a real approval: what the recruiter ticked is exactly what lands, a single disagreeable row no longer forces 'apply all or cancel', and drift between preview and commit is visible instead of silently applied. Also closes the cross-team apply from one team's button.

## Evaluation
Claim: a committed pass applies only the previewed decisions the recruiter kept, and names every one that changed since the preview.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: contract
Result: pending build
Gate: contract
